cards.text: Paul is writing to the church of God in Corinth (2 Cor 1:1). He's just said God qualified him and those with him as ministers of a new covenant, of the Spirit (2 Cor 3:6). Now he looks back at the old one, engraved in letters on stone, and calls it the ministry of death.
But Paul says even that ministry of death came with glory, so much that the Israelites could not gaze at one man's face. Friend, people look away from MY face too, but that's just the mustache.

cards.question: The old covenant on stone came with so much glory that the Israelites couldn't gaze at one man's face. Whose face was it?
Paul says the glory on Moses' face was there to stay.

cards.text: Now Paul starts building, friend. If the ministry of DEATH came with glory like that, then come on now, what about the ministry of the Spirit?

cards.question: The ministry of death came with glory. What does Paul say about the ministry of the Spirit?

answers.text: It will be even more glorious
It will be just as glorious
It will have no glory at all

cards.question: Paul sets the two side by side: the old ministry brings condemnation, and the new ministry brings ___.

cards.text: Paul says what was once glorious has no glory now next to the glory that surpasses it. That's a porch light at noon, friend: still on, still trying, and NOBODY can tell.

cards.question: Paul makes one more comparison. The old glory was fading away. What does he say the new glory does?

cards.text: So Paul and those with him are holding a hope THAT big: a glory that endures. And Paul says a hope like that changes how they carry themselves.

cards.question: Paul says that because he and those with him have the hope of a glory that endures, they are very bold.

cards.text: Then Paul says they are not like Moses, who would put something over his face. Me, I had my face covered for YEARS in that junk drawer, friend, and it was 100 percent dust and zero percent my choice.

cards.question: What would Moses put over his face?
The glory on Moses' face was fleeting. Why does Paul say Moses would put a veil over his face?

answers.text: So the Israelites wouldn't see it end
So the Israelites wouldn't fear him
So the Israelites wouldn't be blinded

cards.text: But Paul says the Israelites' minds were closed, and to this day the same veil remains at the reading of the old covenant. Friend, that veil has hung on longer than the takeout menus in my old junk drawer, and those things NEVER left.

cards.question: Paul says that veil at the reading of the old covenant hasn't been lifted. Where is the only place it can be removed?
Paul says that even to this day, when Moses is read, a veil covers part of the Israelites. What part?
When does Paul say the veil is taken away?

answers.text: Whenever anyone turns to the Lord
Whenever the old glory fades out

cards.question: Paul says the Lord is the Spirit. What does he say is there wherever the Spirit of the Lord is?

cards.text: Then Paul brings it HOME, friend. We all, with unveiled faces, reflect the glory of the Lord. Not just Moses. ALL of us.

cards.question: Paul says something is happening to all of us who reflect the glory of the Lord with unveiled faces. What is it?

answers.text: We are being transformed into His image
We are being sent out to all nations
We are being made ready for His return

cards.question: Paul says the glory we reflect fades away, just like the glory on Moses' face.

cards.text: This glory keeps intensifying, and it comes from the Lord, who is the Spirit. Forget the porch light, friend, THIS is the sun coming up.

findings.problem: The opening names Paul but never simply says who he is. Identifying him as the letter's writer does not give his role; for example, 2 Corinthians 1:1 identifies him as an apostle of Christ Jesus.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: Moses is never given a simple identification. After card 3 supplies his name, this card continues using it without explaining who he is, such as "Moses, Israel's leader."

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The card expressly retells verse 7's ministry of death coming with glory as well as verse 8's comparison, but it cites only 2 Corinthians 3:8. The citation is narrower than the verses the card uses.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The description of the hope as a glory that endures retells verse 11, while the rest of the card retells verse 12. Citing only verse 12 is too narrow for the verses used.

findings.problem: Seven of the nine choice cards are multiple choice, and the other two are true or false. Multiple choice dominates this stop by a wide margin.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has four period-ended sentences or sentence fragments: the opening line, the statement about reflecting glory, "Not just Moses." and "ALL of us." That exceeds the two-sentence limit.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
